evaluation.caveat: Synthetic worlds our own generator wrote (seed_campaign: the seed-42 world plus three call-centre campaigns; seed: the demo world): every till, cash-out and account is generated, and no number here is a field result. A candidate is a lead for an analyst to review, never a verdict or a block. A till flag says only that more confirmed mules cashed out at that till in the last 30 days than its own volume predicts at the network-wide share of seeds (at least TILL_REUSE_MIN_SEEDS of them and a Poisson tail at most TILL_REUSE_P_THRESHOLD): a place to look, not a finding about the agent who runs it. A seed is a mule an analyst confirmed 3 days after its first bad event, while a ring empties its mules within hours: that confirmation lag is why the live 90-minute circle, which needs 3 confirmed mules inside it as it happens, does not fire; the replayed circle uses the seeds known at each day boundary to look back at days already past. Till-flag precision counts only days whose 7-day horizon ends inside the world, beside the base rate of any open till on the same days. The labels are read only by this evaluation and cashout_seeds.py. The Poisson tails assume no over-dispersion, so p-values may be optimistic. For hours in the first week of cash-outs (every till's first week here: all opened before it) the baseline borrows the following weeks (reported as baseline_source: backfill), so a p-value in the first week is not strictly as of the moment; none of the reported clusters falls in a first week. Two candidate filters are measured side by side. The first-time-sender filter (at least CANDIDATE_MIN_FIRST_TIME_SENDERS strangers paying in during the day before the cash-out) was set before any of these numbers and, in its first measurement, named no candidate on either world. The pass-through filter was added after that, because the first filter produced no candidates: money in from at least 1 counterparty the account had not dealt with in 30 days, and cash-outs at least 80% of everything paid in over the same 24 hours. Its constants were fixed in config.py before its own measurement and were not tuned on these numbers, but the decision to add a filter at all followed a result. Both worlds are one synthetic world: seed_campaign is the demo seed plus three campaigns, so the two columns are not independent replications, and one synthetic world is not evidence that either filter works on a real ledger.
